source_title: ODOT CCD Over-Dimension Operations in Oregon (OAR 734-075; Permit Attachment 75-A)
verify_reasons: Pilot-vehicle counts are set per-route on Permit Attachment 75-A (OAR 734-075-0035); the width/height/length thresholds below are ODOT's published 2-lane defaults — confirm the exact per-route configuration through Oregon Trucking Online before dispatch.

Overweight cost is Oregon's weight-mile tax plus a Road Use Assessment Fee (RUAF) for loads over 98,000 lbs; only the $8 flat over-dimension permit fee is codified here, the RUAF is a mileage/weight schedule quoted by ODOT.
Superload has no single fixed gross-weight threshold published; extraordinary weight is handled via RUAF and route/bridge review (gross_weight_lbs left null).

superload_thresholds.note: ODOT superload = over 16' wide (14' wide on 2-lane highways), over 17' high, or 150' long; such moves require extended route evaluation (days to weeks). Extraordinary weight is priced via the Road Use Assessment Fee and bridge review rather than a fixed superload gross number.

width.note: 1 pilot over 12' wide (front on 2-lane, rear on divided highway)
over 16' wide: additional escorts as required on the permit; route review

height.note: over-height pole car in front over 14'6"; may be waived with a signed ODOT liability declaration on file (OAR 734-075-0035)

length.note: over 140': escorts as specified on the permit

single_trip.fee_formula: Over-dimension (oversize) single-trip permit = $8 flat. Overweight is Oregon's weight-mile tax; non-divisible loads over 98,000 lbs GVW pay a Road Use Assessment Fee (RUAF) computed from ODOT's over-98,000 lb mileage/weight tables. Quote via Oregon Trucking Online.
single_trip.note: Single-trip over-dimension permit; overweight fee is schedule-based, not flat. Validity is set per permit.

annual.note: Annual/blanket over-dimension permits available for qualifying repetitive divisible/non-divisible moves; fees vary by class — quote via Oregon Trucking Online.

movement_restrictions: Oversize moves are generally daylight-only (about 1/2 hour before sunrise to 1/2 hour after sunset); loads at or under continuous-travel dimensions may move at night with proper lighting per permit conditions
Loads at superload width/height/length may face weekend, holiday and metropolitan rush-hour curfews specified on the permit
notes: Oregon is a weight-mile-tax state: overweight charges are distance-and-weight based (RUAF over 98,000 lbs), so a gross-weight-only verdict must be treated as indicative — confirm the RUAF quote.
State-level rules only; county/city permits, bridge-specific engineering and low-clearance routing are out of scope.
